name: Processor D
justification: Benchmarking on Processor A revealed severe routing bottlenecks: while simplified 1D nearest-neighbor HEA avoids SWAPs, the complete H2 molecular orbital interaction graph requires all-to-all cross-orbital entanglement across spin-orbitals {0,1,2,3}. On Processor A's acyclic tree topology, executing this complete 6-pair K4 molecular interaction graph forces 2 SWAPs (+6 CX gates, +100% two-qubit overhead, two-qubit depth 12). Processor B's maximum clique is only K3, forcing 1 SWAP (+3 CX, depth 9). Processor D eliminates all routing overhead via an all-to-all K4 chemistry core on qubits {0,1,2,3} with cross-chords (0,2) and (1,3), achieving 0 SWAPs (cx_overhead=0, depth 5) while adhering to a degree <= 4 constraint (unlike B's degree-5 hub on node 6) and matching B's 4 independent loops (9 - 6 + 1 = 4). Qubits 4 and 5 form an ancilla/readout corridor and diagnostic extension for multi-qubit active-space scaling; routing across this diameter-3 corridor incurs 6 extra CX, dropping Bell state fidelity from 0.963 to 0.947, an accepted design trade-off for diagnostic expansion. Error rates match official standards to isolate topological routing gains.
